home.tagline: Cognitive & Affective Computing for Rehabilitation & Embodied Intelligence
home.intro: CARE stands for Cognitive, Affective, Rehabilitation, and Embodied Intelligence. We develop intelligent technologies for older-adult cognitive health, spanning assessment, affective interaction, VR-based training, and companion robots, while supporting student growth through research.
home.systemVideo: Multimodal affective interaction system for cognitive impairment diagnosis and rehabilitation
home.teamIntro: We are a biomedical engineering and AI research group at Nanjing Medical University, working across wearable sensing, emotion recognition, virtual reality rehabilitation, and bionic robotics.
home.vrDesc: Designing immersive rehabilitation scenarios and cognitive tasks that combine behavior, physiology, and interaction data.
home.affectiveDesc: Modeling emotion and mental states through facial, audio, physiological, and contextual signals.
home.embodiedDesc: Building adaptive robotic and embodied systems for natural communication, assistance, and rehabilitation training.
home.launchedDesc: Our new lab website is now online. Stay tuned for updates on research, publications, and lab events.
home.joinDesc: We are looking for motivated students and researchers. Contact us via email for opportunities.

lab.toolsSubtitle: Key tools used in the lab coding workflow for development, file transfer, and remote access.
lab.vscode: Primary code editor with powerful remote development capabilities. Install the Remote-SSH extension to connect directly to lab servers and edit code in a visual environment.
lab.pycharm: Professional Python IDE with excellent debugging, testing, and remote interpreter support. Ideal for Python-heavy research projects and deep learning workflows.
lab.winscp: Reliable file transfer client for uploading code and datasets to remote servers via SFTP/SCP. Provides a familiar Explorer-like interface for managing remote files.
lab.ssh: Secure shell access to lab servers for running code, managing environments, and executing experiments. Can be used via VS Code terminal or standalone SSH clients.
lab.guideSubtitle: Connecting to lab servers via SSH — the primary method for remote development.
lab.method1Help: The most convenient approach — edit server files directly in VS Code with full IDE support.
lab.step1: # 1. Install "Remote - SSH" extension in VS Code
lab.method2Help: Direct terminal connection for running commands and scripts on the server.
lab.terminalHelp: After connection, you can navigate the server file system, run Python scripts, manage GPU resources, and monitor training jobs — all from the terminal.
